source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: The initialized progressive drift has continuous finite-variation paths. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Let the scalar initial value be strongly measurable at time zero and the scalar drift be strongly progressive. Suppose its time section is integrable on the horizon almost surely. The initial value plus the drift integral is strongly progressive and has almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on the horizon. At every sample and time in the horizon it equals the initialized primitive computed with the fixed horizon measure.

T is a nonnegative horizon. The sample space carries a measure and the filtration is indexed by nonnegative time.
The initial value is strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift is strongly progressive, and almost every drift section is integrable against the horizon time measure.

A_t=x+\int_{[0,t]}b(s)\,ds=x+P_b(t),\quad 0\le t\le T.

lean.statement:
theorem anonymous_target.{u_1}
  {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance}
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {T : NNReal} (x : Ω → ℝ) (hx : MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable x) (b : NNReal → Ω → ℝ)
  (hb : MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration b)
  (hbi :
    ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun s => b s ω)
        (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T)) :
  have A := fun t ω =>
    x ω + AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveDriftIntegral.prefixIntegralProcess b t ω;
  MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration A ∧
    (∀ t ≤ T,
        ∀ (ω : Ω),
          A t ω =
            x ω + AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.PrefixIntegral.prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T t) ∧
      ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T) ∧ BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Measurable Omega with arbitrary measure mu and filtration F; initial scalar x; progressive scalar drift b; horizon T; accumulated process A.

x:Omega→R; b:[0,infinity)×Omega→R; T∈[0,infinity). mu is not assumed finite. lambda_t is Lebesgue measure on [0,t], represented on nonnegative reals.

Assumptions: x is strongly measurable with respect to F_0. b is strongly progressive for F. For mu-a.e. omega, b(·,omega) is integrable against lambda_T. No positivity assumption on T.

Conclusion: Define A(t,omega)=x(omega)+∫ b(s,omega) d lambda_t(s). Then A is strongly progressive for F. For every t≤T and every omega, A(t,omega)=x(omega)+∫ 1_{s<min(t,T)}b(s,omega) d lambda_T(s). For mu-a.e. omega, A(·,omega) is continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T].

Quantifier order: For every such x,b,T satisfying the assumptions, all three conclusions hold: progressivity globally; a deterministic all-omega identity for every t≤T; and path continuity plus bounded variation on [0,T] mu-a.e.

Scope: The prefix identity is pointwise for all omega, including exceptional nonintegrable paths, using Lean's total integral convention. Continuity and bounded variation are only almost sure. Progressivity is on all nonnegative times.

Constant dependencies: No existential constants.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveDriftIntegral
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoWeightedRiemannSums

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoInitializedDrift

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open ProgressiveDriftIntegral ItoWeightedRiemannSums
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.PrefixIntegral

/-- The initialized progressive drift has its fixed-horizon primitive
representation and continuous finite-variation paths. -/
theorem initialized_drift_progressive_continuous_boundedVariation
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} {T : ℝ≥0} (x : Ω → ℝ)
    (hx : StronglyMeasurable[filtration 0] x)
    (b : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (hb : IsStronglyProgressive filtration b)
    (hbi : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Integrable (fun s => b s ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T)) :
    let A := fun t ω => x ω + prefixIntegralProcess b t ω
    IsStronglyProgressive filtration A ∧
      (∀ t ≤ T, ∀ ω, A t ω = x ω + prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T t) ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A t ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
        BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A t ω) (Icc 0 T)) := by
  intro A
  have hInitial : StronglyAdapted filtration (fun _ => x) :=
    fun t => hx.mono (filtration.mono (show (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ t from bot_le))
  have hEq (t : ℝ≥0) (ht : t ≤ T) (ω : Ω) :
      prefixIntegralProcess b t ω = prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T t := by
    rw [prefixIntegralProcess_eq_fixedHorizon b ht, prefixIntegral, min_eq_left ht]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun s => by
      by_cases hs : s < t
      · simp only [if_pos hs, min_eq_left (hs.le.trans ht)]
      · simp only [if_neg hs]
  have hAeq (t : ℝ≥0) (ht : t ≤ T) (ω : Ω) :
      A t ω = x ω + prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T t :=
    congrArg (x ω + ·) (hEq t ht ω)
  refine ⟨(hInitial.isStronglyProgressive_of_continuous fun _ => continuous_const).add
    (prefixIntegralProcess_stronglyProgressive b hb), hAeq, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hbi] with ω hω
  let P := prefixIntegral (fun s => b s ω) T
  have hSame : EqOn (fun t => A t ω) (fun t => x ω + P t) (Icc 0 T) :=
    fun t ht => hAeq t ht.2 ω
  refine ⟨(continuous_const.add (continuous_prefixIntegral hω)).continuousOn.congr hSame, ?_⟩
  unfold BoundedVariationOn
  rw [eVariationOn.congr hSame]
  have hVar : eVariationOn (fun t => x ω + P t) (Icc 0 T) =
      eVariationOn P (Icc 0 T) := by
    unfold eVariationOn
    simp only [edist_dist, Real.dist_eq, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
  rw [hVar]
  exact boundedVariationOn_prefixIntegral hω

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoInitializedDrift

steps.title: Use one horizon measure for the time primitive
steps.text: On the active time prefix, clipping the drift's time argument at the horizon leaves it unchanged. The two Lean integral expressions agree at every sample. Almost every sample has an integrable time section, where the expressions have their ordinary integrable-path interpretation.

intro A
  have hInitial : StronglyAdapted filtration (fun _ => x) :=
    fun t => hx.mono (filtration.mono (show (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ t from bot_le))

steps.title: Prove the path properties
steps.text: A time-zero measurable initial value gives a constant progressive process. The integral primitive is progressive, continuous along integrable paths and of bounded variation. Adding the initial value leaves each increment unchanged.

refine ⟨(hInitial.isStronglyProgressive_of_continuous fun _ => continuous_const).add

  rw [eVariationOn.congr hSame]
  have hVar : eVariationOn (fun t => x ω + P t) (Icc 0 T) =

    unfold eVariationOn

  exact boundedVariationOn_prefixIntegral hω

lesson.lean_statement: The result gives progressive measurability, exact fixed-horizon agreement, and almost-everywhere path regularity as three conclusions.
lesson.lean_proof: Move the drift integral to one time measure, apply the existing primitive theorems and use invariance under addition of the initial value.
